key_insight: VideoMLA introduces Multi-Head Latent Attention to video diffusion, replacing expensive per-head key/value caches with a shared low-rank latent cache. This keeps long video generation more memory- and latency-efficient while preserving autoregressive rollout quality.
problem_solved: Long-rollout causal video diffusion models need large KV caches, and the standard fixed-size sliding-window layout consumes too much memory and slows inference. Prior work mostly changed what goes inside the window, but not the per-head KV structure itself.
method: Replace per-head keys and values with a shared low-rank latent representation.
Use this latent KV cache to reduce streaming memory usage and decoding latency during minute-scale autoregressive video generation.
Adapt the attention mechanism for video diffusion so long-context generation can scale more efficiently than standard KV caching.
impact: For practitioners, VideoMLA offers a practical path to longer video rollouts without the usual memory bottlenecks of standard attention caching. It is especially relevant for deploying real-time or resource-constrained video generation systems.
